keywords.def: something that causes another action to start, or speeds it up
used to describe something which shows strong emotion, surprise or excitement
stage when a food item is fully grown and ready for harvest
crush into powder by pressing between two hard surfaces
like, be interested in, or want to do (something)

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Becca. In this episode, we're discussing a food seasoning that's so popular we eat around three quarters of a million tonnes of it a year.
sentences.zh: 我是 Neil。我是 Becca。在本期节目中，我们将讨论一种非常受欢迎的食品调味料，我们每年大约要吃掉 75 万吨。

sentences.en: We're talking about pepper. Do you add pepper to your food, Becca?
sentences.zh: 我们要聊的就是胡椒。Becca，你平时吃东西会加胡椒吗？

sentences.en: I do, Neil, yes. I think it's an easy way to add some spice.
sentences.zh: 我会加的，Neil。我觉得这是增添风味的一种简单方法。

sentences.en: Yeah, I love a bit of pepper. I grind pepper onto everything.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我挺喜欢胡椒的。我吃什么都会研磨点胡椒上去。

sentences.en: Well... not everything! But I do like it.
sentences.zh: 好吧……也不是所有东西！但我确实很喜欢它。

sentences.en: Given its popularity, it's surprising that most people know very little about pepper.
sentences.zh: 鉴于它如此受欢迎，令人惊讶的是大多数人对胡椒其实知之甚少。

sentences.en: Did you know, for example, that peppers are the fruit of vines often growing over ten metres high?
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道胡椒是藤本植物的果实，而且这些藤蔓通常能长到十米以上吗？

sentences.en: Our ancestors would be surprised how little we know.
sentences.zh: 如果我们的祖先知道我们了解得这么少，一定会大吃一惊。

sentences.en: From ancient Greece onwards, pepper was prized as the black gold of ingredients, and explorers crossed oceans in search of it, discovering new continents along the way.
sentences.zh: 从古希腊时代起，胡椒就被尊为食材中的“黑黄金”，探险家们漂洋过海寻找它，并在此过程中发现了新大陆。

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll get reacquainted with pepper and learn some useful new words and phrases too.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将重新认识胡椒，并学习一些实用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember, you'll find a transcript for you to read along with us as you listen, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到听力文本，一边听一边阅读。

sentences.en: OK. First, I have a question for you, of course, Becca.
sentences.zh: 好的。首先，Becca，我当然要问你一个问题。

sentences.en: Although it's black pepper you're most likely to see in shops and restaurants in the UK, there are hundreds of different varieties worldwide.
sentences.zh: 虽然在英国的商店和餐馆中最常见的是黑胡椒，但全世界有数百种不同的胡椒品种。

sentences.en: But what is unusual about Phu Quoc, a white pepper from Vietnam?
sentences.zh: 那么，来自越南的 Phu Quoc 白胡椒有什么不同寻常之处呢？

sentences.en: Does it: a) make people cry, b) taste like parmesan cheese, or c) cost more than gold?
sentences.zh: 它是：a) 让人流泪，b) 尝起来像帕尔马森奶酪，还是 c) 比黄金还贵？

sentences.en: Hmm. Well, I don't think it would be as expensive as gold, and I kind of want it to taste like parmesan cheese.
sentences.zh: 嗯。我觉得它不至于和黄金一样贵，而且我私心希望它尝起来像帕尔马森奶酪。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。我们稍后会在节目中揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Mathilde Roellinger is the daughter of Olivier Roellinger, an award-winning French chef famous for his use of spices.
sentences.zh: Mathilde Roellinger 是 Olivier Roellinger 的女儿，后者是一位屡获殊荣的法国大厨，以善用香料而闻名。

sentences.en: While other little girls of her age were sprinkling sugar on their breakfast yoghurt, Mathilde was the only girl in Paris sprinkling pepper.
sentences.zh: 当同龄的其他小女孩还在往早餐酸奶里撒糖时，Mathilde 是巴黎唯一一个往里面撒胡椒的小女孩。

sentences.en: Today, Mathilde runs the Épices Roellinger spice shop in the Opéra area of the city.
sentences.zh: 如今，Mathilde 在巴黎歌剧院区经营着 Épices Roellinger 香料店。

sentences.en: Here, customers can find a huge range of peppers, from fruity red Cambodian Kampot pepper to Borneo's Sarawak black pepper with its woody aroma.
sentences.zh: 在这里，顾客可以找到琳琅满目的胡椒，从带有果香的柬埔寨贡布红胡椒，到带有木质香气的婆罗洲砂拉越黑胡椒。

sentences.en: These peppers have strong, distinctive tastes, but curiously they enhance rather than overpower the flavour of the food you're eating, as Mathilde explained to BBC World Service programme The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: 这些胡椒具有浓郁而独特的风味，但奇怪的是，它们提升了食物的风味，而不是掩盖它，正如 Mathilde 对 BBC World Service 节目《The Food Chain》所解释的那样。

sentences.en: It will give a kick and transform it, but you will still have the savour of the different ingredients.
sentences.zh: “它会带来一种刺激感并改变风味，但你仍然能尝到不同食材的原汁原味。

sentences.en: It will not disguise the other ingredients, but it will push them – it's a flavour catalyst.
sentences.zh: 它不会掩盖其他食材，而是会推动它们——它是一种风味催化剂。

sentences.en: We can say in punctuation, like it's an exclamation.
sentences.zh: 用标点符号来打比方的话，就像是一个感叹号。”

sentences.en: It's like an exclamation mark. Exactly. Mathilde says pepper gives food a kick.
sentences.zh: 就像一个感叹号。没错。Mathilde 说胡椒能给食物带来一种 kick（刺激感）。

sentences.en: To give something a kick means to provide it with extra stimulation or excitement.
sentences.zh: To give something a kick 意思是给某物带来额外的刺激或兴奋感。

sentences.en: Pepper also makes flavours more intense.
sentences.zh: 胡椒还能让风味更加浓郁。

sentences.en: Mathilde calls it a catalyst – something that causes another action to start or makes it happen more quickly.
sentences.zh: Mathilde 称它为 catalyst（催化剂）——促使另一项行动开始或使其发生得更快的事物。

sentences.en: In fact, she says pepper is like an exclamation mark.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她说胡椒就像一个感叹号。

sentences.en: Saying something is like an exclamation mark means it shows strong emotion or excitement – the same thing an exclamation mark does in written punctuation.
sentences.zh: 说某物 like an exclamation mark（像一个感叹号），意味着它表现出强烈的情感或兴奋——就像标点符号中的感叹号所起的作用一样。

sentences.en: Mathilde's spice shop holds pepper tasting sessions, where she explains to customers the origin of her peppers and how they grow, changing colour as they harden in the sun.
sentences.zh: Mathilde 的香料店会举办胡椒品鉴会，她会向顾客解释胡椒的来源和生长方式，以及它们在阳光下变硬时是如何变色的。

sentences.en: Reporter John Laurenson attended one of these tasting sessions for BBC World Service programme The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: 记者 John Laurenson 为 BBC World Service 节目《The Food Chain》参加了其中一场品鉴会。

sentences.en: The different colours of pepper though, as Mathilde started to say, do not correspond to the different varieties but to the maturity of the peppercorns and what people do to them.
sentences.zh: “不过，正如 Mathilde 开始说的那样，胡椒的不同颜色并不对应不同的品种，而是取决于胡椒粒的成熟度以及人们对它们的处理方式。

sentences.en: They're green when they're young, black when they're mature and dried, red when they're very mature.
sentences.zh: 它们未成熟时是绿色的，成熟并干燥后是黑色的，完全成熟时是红色的。

sentences.en: Grey pepper is an industrial creation, not a botanical one.
sentences.zh: 灰胡椒是一种工业产物，而不是植物学上的产物。

sentences.en: Ground to a fine powder, it is, says Mathilde, grey dust.
sentences.zh: Mathilde 说，把它磨成细粉，就是灰色的尘土。”

sentences.en: She's not very keen on that one. The colour of pepper is not determined by the variety, but by its maturity.
sentences.zh: 她对那种不太感冒。胡椒的颜色不是由品种决定的，而是由它的成熟度决定的。

sentences.en: A food's maturity describes the stage when a food is fully grown and ready to harvest.
sentences.zh: 食物的 maturity（成熟度）描述的是食物完全长大并准备好收获的阶段。

sentences.en: For peppers, this is when they wrinkle and go black.
sentences.zh: 对于胡椒来说，这就是它们起皱变黑的时候。

sentences.en: Often a peppermill is used to grind pepper – to crush it into powder by pressing it between two hard surfaces.
sentences.zh: 人们通常使用胡椒研磨器来 grind（研磨）胡椒——通过在两个坚硬的表面之间挤压将其压碎成粉末。

sentences.en: This happens with grey pepper, an artificially produced pepper mix which Mathilde is not keen on – meaning she doesn't like it.
sentences.zh: 灰胡椒就是这样处理的，它是一种人工制作的混合胡椒，Mathilde 并不 keen on 它——意思就是她不喜欢它。

sentences.en: We've learned so much about pepper, I'll look at it differently the next time I sprinkle some on my food.
sentences.zh: 我们学到了很多关于胡椒的知识，下次我往食物上撒胡椒时，看法肯定会不一样了。

sentences.en: OK. Neil, I think it's time to reveal the answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 好的。Neil，我觉得是时候揭晓你问题的答案了。

sentences.en: Yes, I asked you what's unusual about Phu Quoc, a white pepper from Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 是的，我问你来自越南的 Phu Quoc 白胡椒有什么不同寻常之处。

sentences.en: I answered b) because I want it to taste like parmesan cheese.
sentences.zh: 我选了 b)，因为我希望它尝起来像帕尔马森奶酪。

sentences.en: Well, you're lucky because it is in fact b) it tastes like parmesan cheese.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你很幸运，因为答案确实是 b) 尝起来像帕尔马森奶酪。

sentences.en: Well done. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with the phrase give something a kick – meaning to add extra thrill or excitement.
sentences.zh: 做得好。好的。让我们复习一下今天学到的词汇，首先是短语 give something a kick——意思是增加额外的刺激或兴奋感。

sentences.en: A catalyst causes something to start, or speeds it up.
sentences.zh: catalyst（催化剂）能促使某事开始，或使其加速发生。

sentences.en: If you say something is like an exclamation mark, you mean it signifies strong emotion, surprise or excitement, just like an exclamation mark does in writing.
sentences.zh: 如果你说某物 like an exclamation mark（像一个感叹号），你的意思是它象征着强烈的情感、惊讶或兴奋，就像书写中的感叹号一样。

sentences.en: A food's maturity refers to the stage when it's fully grown and ready for harvest.
sentences.zh: 食物的 maturity（成熟度）指的是它完全长大并准备好收获的阶段。

sentences.en: To grind food means to crush it into powder by being pressed between two hard surfaces.
sentences.zh: grind（研磨）食物意味着通过在两个坚硬表面之间挤压将其压碎成粉末。

sentences.en: And finally, if you're keen on something, you like it and enjoy doing it.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果你 keen on 某事，意思是说你喜欢它并享受做这件事。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember you can find worksheets, quizzes and loads more resources to improve your English on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了，但请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到练习题、测验和更多提高英语水平的资源。

sentences.en: See you there soon, but for now it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 期待很快在网站上见到大家，不过现在要说再见了。

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
